# Hook points and host helpers

Every hook point a native mod (`docs/native-mods.md`) or a trait mod (`crates/horizon-client/src/mod_api.rs`) may listen to, with the API level it arrived in, how it is taken (`listen`: it only hears; `claim`, `cancel`: a mod may stop it; `edit`: every mod changes a value in turn), and the handler a scripted mod (`docs/lua-bindings.md`) registers for it, where one exists. Then every helper the host offers them. The full doc of each is on its `native_<name>` function.

## Hook points

| Hook | API | Taken | Lua | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `add_server_reload_listeners` | 400 | collect |  | The folders of JSON files native mods read from the data (`AddServerReloadListenersEvent`): push yours, each a listener id and a folder under `data/<namespace>/`. Asked at the start of every data load of a server: a world opening, `/reload`. A folder that leaves `data/<namespace>/` is skipped. API 400. |
| `analog_output` | 64 | collect |  | `BlockState.getAnalogOutputSignal`: the signal a comparator reads from the block `state` at `pos`, `face` the side that touches the comparator (or the conductor in front of it). `output` holds vanilla's answer: change it when the block is yours (0 to 15; anything else is clamped). Asked only for blocks `native_has_analog_output` answered for, from inside the level's update: don't change the world here. When the answer changes without the block's state changing, call `native_update_output_neighbors`; a change of state through `native_set_block` or `native_set_block_property` (neighbour updates on) tells the comparators itself, as vanilla's `Level.setBlock` does. Authoritative servers only. API 64. |
| `anvil_craft_post` | — | listen |  | A player took an anvil's result at `pos` and the levels, inputs and anvil wear are done (`AnvilCraftEvent.Post`); a broken anvil is already air. `craft` holds the inputs and the result as they were before. Not called when `native_anvil_craft_pre` cancelled. 327. |
| `anvil_craft_pre` | — | cancel |  | A player took an anvil's result at `pos` (`AnvilCraftEvent.Pre`), before the levels are charged, the inputs used up and the anvil worn. `craft` holds the inputs and the result as they were before. Set `cancel` to refuse the take: the result stays in its slot and the inputs, levels, inventory and cursor are as before the click. 328. |
| `anvil_damaged` | — | listen |  | An anvil at `pos` took damage, changing its block from `from` to `to`. `to` is air when the anvil broke. Server-side. 183. |
| `anvil_update` | — | cancel |  | NeoForge's `AnvilUpdateEvent`: the anvil result of `player` (`name`), where `AnvilMenu.createResult` ends, once vanilla worked it out from the inputs `left` and `right` (none when that slot is empty) and the rename box's `item_name` (NeoForge's `getName`: none until the client sent one, empty to clear a custom name). `vanilla_output`, `vanilla_xp_cost` and `vanilla_material_cost` are vanilla's result (`getVanillaResult`). `output`, `xp_cost` (the level cost) and `material_cost` (how many of `right` the take uses) start as vanilla's, and every mod is called in turn and may change them. Set `canceled` to leave the anvil with no result and both costs at 0: later mods aren't called. A negative level cost becomes 0 (`AnvilMenu.setCost`), and a result that costs 0 levels can't be taken. A material cost of 0 or less, or one above what `right` holds, takes the whole stack (none when the anvil only renames). Asked whenever the inputs or the name change while the left slot holds an item, on the `Game` that works out the result: a host's (single player's server thread, a LAN or dedicated host) for each player's menu, and the window's own, so a mod answers alike on both sides to keep the window in step with the server. The window works its result out again after each click in the menu, so it may ask about the same inputs again: a mod should answer from what it is told. On the host, `native_prepare_anvil` comes after it. API @API:anvil_update@. |
| `apply_effect_tick` | 56 | listen |  | `MobEffect.applyEffectTick`: the content mod's effect `effect` acts on `entity` in `dimension` (`minecraft:overworld`). Clear `keep` and the effect ends now, before it counts down. `entity` is a mob's `Entity.getId`, None for a player (`native_acting_player` says who). It runs inside the entity's tick: a mob's world borrows the game there, so the game is read-only, and it does not hold the ticking mobs, nor the player's effects. Server-side. API 56. |
| `armor_stand_manipulate` | — | cancel |  | A player takes an item from an armor stand or puts one on it (`ArmorStand.interactAt`, after the stand's disabled-slot checks and `swapItem`'s take/put locks, before anything moves): `stand_id` is the stand's `Entity.getId` and `slot` the one the click reached (`mainhand`, `offhand`, `feet`, `legs`, `chest` or `head`). Set `cancel` and nothing changes: neither the stand nor the player's hand, and the click is spent. The player's state is swapped in for the call; `player` is the UUID the helpers take. Not told of a click that changes nothing (an empty hand on an empty slot). Not covered, other ways a stand's equipment moves: breaking or blasting the stand (its items drop), a dispenser putting armour on one, a mod's own changes. Server-side, for every player of the world. 175. |
| `arrow_loose` | — | cancel |  | NeoForge's `ArrowLooseEvent`: the player releases a bow `stack` with `has_ammo` and `charge` ticks held. Change `charge` or set `canceled` to prevent the shot; negative charge also prevents it. Unlike `native_living_entity_use_item_stop`, this does not skip the whole item release; `native_entity_shoot_bow` reports a spawned arrow afterward with read-only force. Fires on the Game running the bow release, including LAN guests; a remote client's own release path is not covered. Crossbows are not covered; `native_arrow_nock` is the bow's start. 318. |
| `arrow_nock` | — | cancel |  | A player is about to nock `bow` with `hand` (`BowItem.use`, NeoForge's `ArrowNockEvent`): `has_ammo` is whether `getProjectile` found ammunition or the player is in creative. Set `cancel` to fail the use. 375. |
| `attack_entity` | 22 | cancel | `item_hit(item, player, target)`, by held item | A player attacks the entity `entity` (`Entity.getId`) of type `kind` (`minecraft:item_frame`, `minecraft:cow`, `minecraft:player`) standing at `pos`: `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleInteract`'s attack, once in reach, where `Player.attack` starts. Set `canceled` and the blow does nothing (no damage, no knockback, the frame keeps its item). Server-side, for every player of the world (`native_acting_player` says who). API 22. |
| `baby_entity_spawn` | 395 | cancel |  | Two animals bred and a baby is about to be made (NeoForge's `BabyEntitySpawnEvent`, vanilla's `Animal.spawnChildFromBreeding`): `parent` and `partner` are entity ids, `player` the UUID of the player who fed them into love (0 when none), `kind` the baby's type (a horse and a donkey have a mule). Set `cancel` for no baby: the parents still rest and lose their love (their ages were already set to 6000), but there is no baby, no experience, no `animals_bred` statistic, no advancement and no heart particles, as NeoForge returns before `finalizeSpawnChildFromBreeding`. Not fired for turtles, frogs and sniffers (an egg, no baby), villagers or armadillos' own paths. On the server. API 395. |
| `beacon_state_change` | — | listen |  | A beacon at `pos` activated or deactivated after its beam was checked. `active` says whether it now has a complete pyramid. Server-side. 184. |
| `bell_ring` | — | cancel |  | On an authoritative server, a bell at `pos` is about to ring. Set `cancel` to stop the ring and its raider reveal. 185. |
| `biome_colors` | 107 | listen |  | Change the colours of `biome` (`minecraft:plains`) on this client: the grass, foliage (leaves, vines), dry foliage (leaf litter) and water tints, 0xRRGGBB, as its biome file and the colormaps set them. Asked for every biome when a mod calls `native_refresh_biome_colors`, which rebuilds the terrain with them; a season mod answers from its season and calls that when the season turns. The dark forest's modifier still applies to the grass set here; the swamp's noise colours replace it. API 107. |
| `block_break_progress_update` | — | listen |  | A server guest's block-breaking animation changed to `progress` at `pos` (0 through 9). 186. |
| `block_burn` | — | cancel |  | On an authoritative server, fire is about to burn the block at `pos` away. Set `cancel` to keep that block. 187. |
| `block_changed` | — | listen |  | An authoritative server committed a changed state through `Level.setBlock`. The world contains `new`; block side effects and neighbour updates follow. |
| `block_clone_item` | — | replace |  | A block's clone item before Ctrl+Pick adds block-entity components. The first supplied stack replaces the block's normal clone item; no response keeps vanilla behavior. Empty or unregistered replacements produce no picked item, including for a block without a primary item. @API:block_clone_item@ |
| `block_cook` | — | listen |  | A block finished cooking `item` into `result` at `pos`. 188. |
| `block_damage_abort` | — | listen |  | A server player stopped digging `pos` before the block broke, after the server cleared the dig and sent the block back to the client. The player's state is not swapped in. 329. |
| `block_dispense_armor` | — | listen |  | A dispenser equipped `item` on the first eligible `target` in front of its block at `pos`. `target` is `player`, `mob` or `armor_stand`. The equip, item consumption, sound and game event have completed. Server-side. 189. |
| `block_entity` | 15 | replace | `horizon.block_entity(block, { ticks, data })` | Block `block` (`mymod:machine`) gets a block entity (`EntityBlock.newBlockEntity`): set `entity` to its id and saved compound when the block is yours and `entity` is none yet. It works on any template: the engine removes the block entity when its block is broken or replaced, no piston moves it, and a mod that draws it (`native_block_entity_submit`) is asked for it. API 15; before 129 the block's template had to have a block entity of its own (a chest, a furnace...), or the block got none. |
| `block_entity_accepts_fluid` | — | cancel |  | Does tank `tank` of the mod block `block` take `fluid` (`minecraft:water`, `minecraft:lava`, or a mod's own, `create:chocolate`)? NeoForge's `IFluidHandler.isFluidValid`: a water tank refuses a mod's fluid, so a removed mod leaves no id it cannot use behind. Asked on the server before `native_fluid_insert` fills a tank that the block's `ModFluidTanks` lets be filled through that face, in both passes (same fluid first, then empty), and before `native_move_fluids` counts that tank's room. Set `cancel` to refuse the fluid there; the fill tries the next tank. Every tank accepts every fluid unless a mod says otherwise; a cauldron, which holds only water and lava, and a drain never ask it. Bundles need "hooks": @API:block_entity_accepts_fluid@. |
| `block_entity_container` | 17 | replace |  | Block `block`'s block entity has item slots (a `WorldlyContainer`): set `container` when the block is yours. Asked once for each mod block when the ticking table is built; at most 256 slots, and slot numbers past the count are left out. Its `menu`, one of `containers::MOD_MENUS` or a content mod's menu type (`data/<id>/horizon/menu/`, API 85) with as many slots, opens when the block is used (its template must open a menu, as a chest or a furnace does); another is left out. A mod menu type shows on Horizon clients through the mod's `native_screen` only. API 17. |
| `block_entity_energy` | 142 | replace |  | Block `block`'s block entity has an energy buffer (`Capabilities.Energy.BLOCK`): set `energy` when the block is yours, as `SimpleEnergyHandler` is built: its capacity, the most one insert and one extract moves, and the faces a fill may come through and a drain may leave by. Asked once for each mod block when the ticking table is built; a capacity under 1 leaves the buffer out, and the limits are clamped to 0..=capacity. The amount is kept in the entity's saved compound, as the int `energy`, and the energy helpers below read and write it. API 142. |
| `block_entity_fluids` | 54 | replace |  | Block `block`'s block entity has fluid tanks: set `fluids` when the block is yours, in the container's shape — each tank's capacity in millibuckets, the tanks each face reaches, and the tanks a fill may reach and a drain may take. Asked once for each mod block when the ticking table is built; at most 16 tanks, capacities clamped to 1..=1 000 000, and tank numbers past the count are left out. The tanks' contents are kept in the entity's saved compound, under `fluids`, and the fluid helpers below read and write them. API 54. |
| `block_entity_inside` | — | listen |  | `Block.entityInside` for each mod block touched along the entity's movement. Repeated sweep hits in one contact pass are suppressed; idle overlap still fires. |
| `block_entity_render_bounding_box` | 71 | collect |  | Where the mod block entity at `pos` draws, for culling (NeoForge's `getRenderBoundingBox`): `bounds` is min x, y, z then max x, y, z, in blocks from the block's lower north-west corner. It starts as the block with a block of margin around it; widen it when your `native_block_entity_submit` draws further (a tall shaft, a beam), or set an infinite value for one never culled. Asked once a frame for each within 64 blocks whose chunk is drawn. API 71. |
| `block_entity_submit` | 71 | listen |  | Draw the mod block entity at `pos`, of block `block` (`mymod:machine`), on this client: once a frame while it is in view (vanilla's `BlockEntityRenderer.submit`: within 64 blocks, its chunk faded in, and its bounds, `native_block_entity_render_bounding_box`, in the frustum), when its `id` is yours. `state` is the block's state (`blockEntity.getBlockState()`: read its `facing` with `native_block_state_property`), `entity` holds what the server sent (`native_block_entity_update_tag`). Add geometry with `native_draw_quad`, `native_draw_cube`, `native_draw_block` and `native_draw_item` under `draw`'s pose stack, which starts at the block's lower north-west corner, in blocks; `draw` also has the partial tick, the game time and the block's light. API 71. |
| `block_entity_tick` | 17 | listen | `block_entity_tick(dimension, block, x, y, z, data)`, by block | A server tick of the block entity at `pos`, in vanilla's order among the others (`Level.tickBlockEntities`), when its `id` is yours: read and change its saved compound `nbt`, its item slots `items` (keep their count: as many as its container has, none without one) and the data slots its menu shows (`data`). It is out of the world during the call (the block entity at `pos` reads as a `Mod` with an empty id, and a save leaves it out); if the call removes or replaces it, `entity` is dropped. Clients, the window's own in single player included, get what `native_block_entity_update_tag` gives when its chunk is sent or its block changes. API 17. |
| `block_entity_ticks` | 15 | listen | `horizon.block_entity(block, { ticks = true })` | Whether block `block`'s block entity ticks (`EntityBlock.getTicker`): set `ticks` when it is yours. Asked for each of the block's states when a world opens. API 15. Set `ticks` to true to make it tick, and never clear a value an earlier mod or mixin set. |
| `block_entity_update_tag` | 45 | replace |  | What clients get of the block entity at `pos` when its `id` is yours (`BlockEntity.getUpdateTag`): set `tag` to it, read from `entity` alone. Asked on the server whenever a chunk holding it is sent and whenever its block changes, on the server thread or, for a saved chunk sent past the view distance (`lan::far`), another one; a client's copy of the block entity (made by `native_block_entity` there) merges it into its `nbt`. Leave it unset to send nothing. API 45. |
| `block_exp` | — | listen |  | A broken block is about to drop `experience` points at `pos`. The vanilla block drop rule has been checked; change the amount before its orbs are awarded. Server-side. 190. |
| `block_fade` | — | cancel |  | A block at `pos` is about to fade from `from` to `to` because of melting or coral death. Set `cancel` to keep it. Server-side. 191. |
| `block_failed_dispense` | — | listen |  | A dispenser at `pos` failed to dispense `item`. Server-side. 192. |
| `block_fall_on` | — | collect |  | `Block.fallOn` for a mod block. Change calculated damage before generic fall sounds and hurt handling; zero prevents both. Creative and fall-immune entities notify with zero damage and retain their immunity. Server-side only. |
| `block_form` | — | cancel |  | Precipitation is about to form or add to a block at `pos`. `from` and `to` are block state IDs. Set `cancel` to keep the old state. Server-side. 193. |
| `block_highlight` | — | cancel |  | Before an eligible targeted block's selection outline is built. Cancel skips only the default block highlight, after normal HUD and game-mode gates. |
| `block_ignite` | — | cancel |  | On an authoritative server, fire is about to be placed at `pos` by flint and steel, a fire charge, lava, lightning or fire spread. Set `player` is the acting server player when there is one. Set `cancel` to leave the position unchanged. 194. |
| `block_lock_check` | — | cancel |  | A guest's block inventory lock check at `pos`. `locked` is the vanilla result and may be changed. The guest's state is not swapped in. 195. |
| `block_place` | — | cancel |  | A guest is about to place `stack` as the block `state` at `pos`: where `BlockItem.place` has found the position and the state and checked that the block survives there unobstructed, before anything is set (Bukkit's `BlockPlaceEvent`, NeoForge's `BlockEvent.EntityPlaceEvent`). Set `cancel` and nothing is placed or used (a failed placement): the client sees the blocks and its inventory as they are, and `native_place_block` hears nothing. The guest's state is swapped in. `state` is `getStateForPlacement`'s, before the stack's `block_state` component; finding it asks `native_state_for_placement` and `native_can_survive` once more. Server-side, guests only. @API:block_place@. |
| `block_receive_game` | — | cancel |  | A sculk sensor or shrieker received a vibration for `event` at `pos`. Set `cancel` to suppress its response. Server-side. 196. |
| `block_redstone` | — | listen |  | The button, lever or pressure plate at `pos` is about to change its signal from `old` to `new` (0 to 15; Bukkit's `BlockRedstoneEvent`): a button pressed or let go (by a hand, an arrow or its release tick), a lever pulled, a plate's weight checked. Change `new` and the component takes that signal instead, clamped to 0 to 15: one equal to `old` keeps it as it is (a held button's release is scheduled again, a plate held on is checked again, a lever stays; no sound), and an on-or-off component is on for anything above 0. Not heard: redstone wire, torches, repeaters, comparators, observers, detector rails, tripwire hooks, daylight detectors and the other signal sources. Server-side. @API:block_redstone@. |
| `block_shear_entity` | — | listen |  | A dispenser sheared `entity` of kind `kind` at the block in front of its own block at `pos`, after the shearing effects. Server-side. 197. |
| `block_signal` | 38 | listen |  | The redstone signal the block `state` at `pos` gives on its `face`, the side that touches the block reading it: `BlockState.getDirectSignal` when `direct` (what passes through a block it touches, as a lever's does), else `getSignal`. `signal` holds vanilla's answer: change it when the block is yours (0 to 15; anything else is clamped). Asked very often, from inside the level's update, so answer from your own state: check the block first, and don't read or change the world here. When the answer changes, and once the block is placed, call `native_update_signal_neighbors`. Authoritative servers only. API 38. |
| `block_spread` | 22 | cancel |  | On an authoritative server, a fluid flows or fire spreads from `from` into `to` (`kind` is `fluid` or `fire`): `FlowingFluid.spreadTo`, and `FireBlock.tick` setting fire to `to` or burning it (`checkBurnOut`). Set `canceled` to leave the block at `to` as it is. Fluids ask on every flow: answer fast. API 22. |
| `block_step_on` | — | listen |  | `Block.stepOn` for a mod block, on its authoritative server level. No self: the simulation owns the entity during this callback. |
| `blocks` | 145 | collect |  | Blocks this mod adds, declared in code rather than one file each (NeoForge's `DeferredRegister.Blocks` drained by `RegisterEvent`): push a `horizon_mods::content::Block` per block, the same declaration a content mod's `data/<id>/horizon/block/<path>.json` holds (a vanilla `template`, `properties`, `state_properties`, `shapes`...), with its id in your mod's namespace. `item: true` gives it a block item, as a file does unless told not to (`..Default::default()` leaves it false). They join the content mods' blocks: the one whose id is that namespace when it is on (your models, textures, loot and recipes are its files), else one of their own, with the template's look. Ids, saves and the check that a joining client has the same blocks are the files' (docs/mods.md). Asked once at start, on every side, before any resource loads: push the same ones every time, from nothing but your code. Declarations that don't pass the files' checks are logged and that namespace's are left out. API 145. |
| `break_speed` | — | listen |  | NeoForge's `PlayerEvent.BreakSpeed`: how fast the player digs the block `state` at `pos`, where `Player.getDestroySpeed` ends. `speed` starts as vanilla's, `original` (the tool, mining efficiency, Haste and Mining Fatigue, the block break speed attribute, the slowdowns under water and off the ground), and a mod may change it; every mod is called in turn, and `original` stays vanilla's. `BlockBehaviour.getDestroyProgress` then divides the speed by the block's hardness and by 30, or 100 without the right tool, for each tick of the dig: a speed of 0 makes no progress, so the block isn't broken, not even one that breaks at once. Not asked for an unbreakable block (hardness -1) nor in creative mode. Fires on the `Game` that works out the dig: single player's, a LAN or dedicated host's for each guest (the helpers read that player), and a remote client's own prediction, so a mod changes the speed alike on both sides to keep the crack in step with the server. It is asked every tick of a dig, on each side, so it should only compute. API @API:break_speed@. |
| `brewing_complete` | — | listen |  | A brewing stand finished brewing at `pos`, after its bottle contents were changed. Server-side. 198. |
| `brewing_fuel` | — | listen |  | A brewing stand at `pos` consumed `fuel` and gained brewing fuel. Server-side. 199. |
| `brewing_start` | — | listen |  | A brewing stand at `pos` began brewing `ingredient`, after fuel and the timer were set. Server-side. 200. |
| `broadcast_message` | — | cancel |  | A server broadcast line is about to be logged and sent. Change `line` or set `cancel` to drop it. 201. |
| `bucket_empty` | — | cancel |  | A server player empties a bucket at `pos` (`fluid`: `minecraft:water`, `minecraft:lava`, `minecraft:powder_snow`; a fish or axolotl bucket empties `minecraft:water`): where `BucketItem.use` has found the block the fluid goes into and the player may build there, right before it is placed. Set `cancel` and nothing is poured and the bucket stays full. The player's state is swapped in, so `native_tell` answers them. Only for guests of a server. `native_fill_bucket` hears this click too (and the filling one) without the player and the fluid. Not heard: a dispenser, a cauldron, and a fluid a block places itself. 179. |
| `camera_distance` | — | listen |  | Final scaled third-person camera distance, before visual-shape collision clipping. `entity` includes its living scale/distance and optional mount scale/distance. Only finite requests in 0..=1024 blocks replace the vanilla distance. |
| `camera_pose` | 402 | listen |  | The camera this frame is drawn from, `partial` ticks past the last tick, after vanilla placed it (`Camera.setup`): its position, and its yaw and pitch in degrees. Set them to draw the world from anywhere: a cinematic or replay camera. Only the picture, the sound's listener and the billboards facing the camera follow it; the player, where they aim, the first-person hand and which chunks load stay the player's. Values that aren't finite keep vanilla's. Not called on the title screen's panorama. API 402. |
| `camera_shake` | 82 | listen |  | The camera shake native mods ask for in this frame, `partial` ticks past the last tick (0 to 1): add your pitch, yaw and roll in degrees and your offset in blocks, along the camera's right, up and back, to `shake`, so several mods' shakes add up. Read while playing only; Horizon scales the sum by Distortion Effects and bounds it (`native_shake_matrix`). API 82. |
| `campfire_start` | — | listen |  | An item was placed on a campfire at `pos` and began cooking. 202. |
| `can_eat` | 90 | listen |  | `Player.canEat` for the food `stack`, from `Consumable.canConsume` when eating starts: `can_eat` arrives with vanilla's (creative, `can_always_eat`, or hungry). Clear it to refuse the food, set it to let a full player eat. Both sides (the client starts eating as the server does), so answer from the stack and the player alone. API 90. |
| `can_player_sleep` | 393 | listen |  | A server player tries to sleep in the bed whose head is at `pos` (NeoForge's `CanPlayerSleepEvent`, vanilla's `ServerPlayer.startSleepInBed`). `problem` is what vanilla found, first problem only: `too_far_away`, `obstructed`, `not_possible_now` (not night or thunder, the bed rule), `not_safe` (monsters near), or `None`. A mod may set `None` to let the player sleep anyway, or one of those names (`other_problem` refuses without a message) to refuse. The spawn point is set before it fires, as in vanilla, only when vanilla found no problem. After it, `native_player_bed_enter` still fires and may cancel. Server-side. API 393. |
| `can_survive` | 70 | replace |  | On an authoritative server, `BlockState.canSurvive` for `state` at `pos` (`BlockBehaviour.canSurvive`), before the block answers it: as it is placed (`BlockItem.canPlace`), from a shape update of a block whose template checks it (a plant, a torch, a sign: false breaks the block with its drops), and wherever else vanilla asks. `state` may not be in the world yet, so decide from `state`. Answer only for your own blocks: `Some(false)` refuses the spot, `Some(true)` allows it, and the block's own rule doesn't run. The level is read-only. Asked on every shape update of such a block: keep it short. API 70. |
| `cauldron_level_changed` | — | cancel |  | On an authoritative server, a cauldron at `pos` is about to change fill level from `from_level` to `to_level` for `reason`. Set `cancel` to leave it unchanged. 203. |
| `chorus_fruit_teleport` | — | cancel |  | A server player who ate chorus fruit (or another item with the `teleport_randomly` consume effect) is about to try a random spot (NeoForge's `EntityTeleportEvent.ChorusFruit`, vanilla's `TeleportRandomlyConsumeEffect.apply`): once per attempt (up to 16), after they stopped riding. `from` is their feet, `target` the spot drawn; a mod may move it (its y kept inside the level's height, a value that is not a number ignored), and the game still looks down from it for ground it may land on. Canceling ends the effect: no teleport and no more attempts. The player's state is swapped in (`native_acting_player`). Foxes are not heard. 311. |
| `chunk_generate` | — | listen |  | A native mod's hook point (docs/native-mods.md), listed in `native-hooks.json` with the game's: chunk `[x, z]` of the level `dimension` (`minecraft:overworld`) is about to get its terrain, after its biomes and structure starts and before the noise (Bukkit's `ChunkGenerator.generateNoise`; vanilla's `ChunkStatus.NOISE`). `seed` is the world's (`native_world_seed`); `flat` says the level is superflat (its layers stand where the noise would). A mod that builds the chunk sets its blocks with `chunk_out.set_block` (all air until then) and sets `generate` to `Replaced`, whose flags say what vanilla adds: the surface rule, the carvers (on a superflat level too), the structures, the features. Leave `generate` at `Vanilla` and set no block to keep vanilla's terrain; `set_biomes` and `clear_structures` work with either answer. Mods are asked in turn and see what earlier ones set. Called on the generation workers, for several chunks at once on several threads and never on the server thread: keep what the mod reads `Sync`, and no `Game` helper works here. A chunk can be asked again (a proto chunk saved unfinished, the neighbours of a finished chunk, the far terrain's decoration), so answer the same each time. API 108. |
| `server_packet` | — | cancel |  | A play packet the server is about to send `player`'s client (ProtocolLib's and PacketEvents' outgoing packet listener; there is no NeoForge or Bukkit event): every packet the server sends a guest in play, a broadcast once for each of its players, in the order they are sent, decoded (`ClientboundPlayPacket`). Change `packet` and the client gets the changed one instead, encoded again; set `cancel` and that client gets nothing. Heard only after a mod called `native_watch_server_packets`: until then the server neither decodes nor copies what it sends. Not heard: the configuration phase, the disconnect a kick sends, a packet whose bytes don't decode (it goes out as it was), and a player who isn't a guest (single player's own). It runs where the packet is sent, on whichever server thread sends it, once a packet and player, so it should be cheap; there is no `self` and no player's state is swapped in. Server-side. @API:server_packet@. |
| `server_packets` | — | listen |  | Once a server tick, after `ServerTickEnd`, the play packets one player's connection sent (`outbound`) or received since the last tick while a mod counts them (`native_count_packets(true)`; off, nothing is kept and this never fires): each as (packet id, body bytes) in order, the id of `horizon_protocol::ids::play` as the server sent or read it (before an older client's renumbering, keep-alives and the disconnect included) and the bytes of id and payload, before compression and encryption, as PacketEvents counts them. Called at most twice a tick per player, only with packets; a stalled tick keeps at most 65536 each way. PacketEvents' send and receive events, batched. API @API:server_packets@. |
| `server_reload_listener_apply` | 400 | listen |  | A listener's files were read (`SimpleJsonResourceReloadListener`'s `apply`): `files` holds `<namespace>:<path>` (the file's path under the folder, without `.json`) and its JSON, sorted by id, from the resource root (vanilla's and content mods' data) and the world's enabled data packs; for each id the top pack's file, and a file that isn't JSON is logged and left out. Every mod hears every listener, so check `listener.id`. Fired on each data load before `native_server_data_loaded`. Server-side. API 400. |
| `server_stopping` | 44 | listen |  | The server begins an orderly stop (NeoForge's `ServerStoppingEvent`): the start of vanilla's `MinecraftServer.stopServer`, with the worlds still loaded and the players still connected and not yet saved, so a mod can save its own data or tell them. `native_world_lifecycle`'s `WorldCloseFinal` follows once the worlds are saved. A server whose loop fails stops without this (`WorldCloseFailed` reports it). API 44. |
| `server_tick` | — | listen | `server_tick(phase, world_running)` | The authoritative server tick's phases: `ServerTickStart` before any level is ticked (NeoForge's `ServerTickEvent.Pre`), `ServerTickEnd` after the last (`.Post`). Read blocks with `native_server_block`, by dimension: which level `self.world` holds here is not defined. A paused pass fires nothing; a frozen world carries `world_running` false except during a requested step. |
| `server_tick_timed` | — | listen |  | After each pass of the server tick (paused ones too) while its spans are recorded: always on a dedicated server, whose slow-tick log keeps them on, elsewhere while `native_spans(true)`, `HORIZON_SPIKES` or a performance report asks for them. `wall_ms` is the pass's wall time, `cpu_ms` the server thread's CPU time in it (None where the system doesn't tell), and `spans` its named steps, summed by name in the order first seen, each with its depth (`tick_mobs` inside `tick`): what a profiler such as spark samples, by step instead of stack. The tick's own clock (`native_tick_times`) also counts the work after the pass (the idle kick, the next tick's wait). API @API:server_tick_timed@. |
| `settings` | — | collect |  | The buttons of mod `mod_id`'s settings page, under its keys: push their labels when it is yours. Asked again each time the page opens and after each click. |
| `settings_click` | — | listen |  | Button `button` of mod `mod_id`'s settings page was clicked. |
| `shader_params` | 84 | listen |  | The values native mods hand their shader packs in this frame, `partial` ticks past the last tick (0 to 1): a pack's WGSL reads them as `frame.mods` (eight `vec4<f32>`). Write the slots your own pack reads; a mod that bundles its pack as `native-<mod id>` is the one that pack is for. Asked once a frame while a pack is on; a value that isn't finite reads as 0 (`native_shader_params_now`). API 84. |
| `should_apply_effect_tick_this_tick` | 56 | listen |  | `MobEffect.shouldApplyEffectTickThisTick` for a content mod's effect `effect` (`ruby:bleeding`), each tick a player or a mob has it, in `MobEffectInstance.tickServer` before it counts down: `tick_count` is the ticks left (the entity's tick count when infinite). Set `apply` and `native_apply_effect_tick` follows. Server-side. API 56. |
| `sign_changed` | — | cancel |  | A player finished editing a sign: `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.updateSignText` has taken their update packet and every check has passed (they were editing that sign, within reach, the sign is not waxed, the chat filter let the text through), right before the lines go on the sign. `pos` in `dimension`, the `front` or back side, and the four `lines` as written, plain text with the formatting codes still in (vanilla strips them afterwards). Rewrite `lines` (made four lines again) and that is what the sign gets, without a second look from the chat filter, or set `cancel` and the sign keeps its old text. With the player's state swapped in, so `native_tell` and the helpers that act on the player reach them. Once for each update a player sends on a server. Not told: the host's own editing of a sign on a LAN or single-player world (the editor writes into their world directly), and the sign changes that are no edit of the text (dyeing, glow ink, waxing, `/data`, `/setblock`, mods' `native_with_mod_block_entity`). 150. |
| `sleep_finished_time` | 308 | listen |  | Enough players have slept through the night in level `dimension` and the clock is about to move to the morning (NeoForge's `SleepFinishedTimeEvent`, vanilla's `ServerLevel.tick` when it moves the clock to `wake_up_from_sleep`): `new_time` comes in as the next morning's day time and may be changed to wake everyone at another time. A time before `current` (the day time now) is refused, as `setTimeAddition` refuses one, and the morning stays. Unlike NeoForge, which refuses a bad value as it is set, the check runs once after every mod, so a later mod sees the value an earlier one left. On the server, only when the `advance_time` rule is on; `native_time_skip` then hears the jump to the time chosen here and may still cancel it. The players wake and the weather resets as usual either way. API 308. |
| `smoke_source` | 157 | replace |  | On an authoritative server, `CampfireBlock.isSmokeSource` for the block `state` under a campfire, as the campfire is placed or the block under it changes: `Some(true)` for your own blocks makes the campfire a signal fire whose smoke rises higher, as over a hay bale. The level is read-only. API 157. |
| `sound_play` | — | cancel |  | A client sound is about to start or update (`sound.starting`). Change `volume`/`pitch` or cancel before subtitles and backend writes. Parameters are the instance's base values, before the chosen file's random samples, category/master gain and ordinary pitch clamps. Edits are transient: tickable updates and loop replays start from current unmodified values. Changed values must be finite, volume nonnegative and pitch positive; invalid edits cancel that operation (an update stops the sound). No Host, world borrow or reverb/DSP surface is supplied. Runs on the game thread. API @API:sound_play@. |
| `spawn_change` | — | listen |  | The world's spawn point changed to `pos` and `angle`. 244. |
| `sponge_absorb` | — | listen |  | A sponge at `pos` absorbed water and became wet. Server-side. 297. |
| `standalone_models` | 151 | collect |  | Models no blockstate names that this client bakes beside the block models (NeoForge's `ModelEvent.RegisterStandalone`): push their ids (`mymod:block/shaft_half`, the model at `assets/mymod/models/block/shaft_half.json`). Parts a block entity or a mob draws, with `native_draw_model`, so that no block is registered only to bake its model. Asked once at start, before the resources load; every resource load, a pack reload included, bakes them again from that pack's files. A model that doesn't read is logged and left out; an id without a namespace is dropped. Every side asks it, but only a window bakes models. API 151. |
| `state_for_placement` | — | replace |  | A block is about to take the state it is placed in (`Block.getStateForPlacement(BlockPlaceContext)`), `state` the block's own default state. Answer only for your blocks: put the state you want in `answer` as `Some(Some(state))` — a state of that block, as vanilla sets properties on its own `defaultBlockState` (another block's is ignored) — or refuse the placement with `Some(None)`: the block goes nowhere and the stack is kept, as vanilla's `null`. Left empty, the block's own placement runs. `context` is vanilla's `BlockPlaceContext` (the clicked face, the placer's rotation, the clicked position, whether the clicked block is being replaced, the item in hand) and `fluid` the fluid in the position the block would go in, which a waterlogged block reads. Build the state from `state` with `native_state_with_property`, and know whether `state` is yours with `native_state_block`. It is asked for every placer that goes through vanilla's placement (a player's `BlockItem.place`, a dispenser's `DirectionalPlaceContext`), and the answer still takes its survival and entity obstruction checks. A trait mod returns `Some(Some(state))` to choose a state, `Some(None)` to refuse, or `None` to leave the answer to the next mod or vanilla. Authoritative servers only. 76. |
| `tab_complete` | — | collect |  | A guest asked to complete `command`; `suggestions` may be added to or filtered. `range` is the replaced byte range. 298. |
| `tab_complete_v2` | — | collect |  | `native_tab_complete` with the command split as Bukkit's `TabCompleter.onTabComplete` gets it, heard right after it: `label` is the command's first word and `arguments` the words after it, split at each space, the last the one being typed (empty after a space; none while the label is typed). For a command a mod registered (`native_register_commands`) the client asks only for an argument whose kind asks the server (`word?`, `text?`, `player_name`); `range` is then the word being typed, and for `player_name` `suggestions` already holds the online players' names matching it. Push yours over `range`. No player's state is swapped in and the server's players are out of reach (`native_server_players` gives none). Server-side. API @API:tab_complete_v2@. |
| `target_hit` | — | listen |  | A projectile hit the target block at `pos`, which now has `strength` output power. Server-side. 299. |
| `thunder_change` | — | cancel |  | The server changed its thunder state through `/weather`. Set `cancel` to keep the previous thunder state and timer. Server-side. 300. |
| `tick` | — | listen |  | Once a tick, in every `Game`: the window's (in single player, on LAN and on servers), and the server's own (`native_window` is false there: the single player server thread, a dedicated server). |
| `tick_block` | — | cancel | `tick_block(dimension, block, x, y, z, props, data)`, by block | An authoritative server's `ServerLevel.tickBlock` is about to run a due scheduled tick of the block `state` at `pos` (`BlockState.tick`): the block is still the one the tick was scheduled for. Change the block with `native_set_block_property` and set `handled` to skip the block's own tick; a block changed without `handled` takes its own tick as it is now, if it is still the tick's block. |
| `time_skip` | — | cancel |  | The overworld clock is about to jump, from sleep or `/time`. Set `cancel` to keep `from`. 301. |
| `tnt_primed` | — | cancel |  | TNT at `pos` is about to be lit (primed): a flint and steel or a fire charge on it, fire burning it, a redstone signal, an arrow, or a dispenser's flint and steel or TNT item. `player` is the server player whose click lit it, with their state swapped in (so `native_tell` answers them), None when no player is behind it (fire, redstone, an arrow, a dispenser). Set `cancel` and it is not primed: a TNT block stays where it is (one that fire or a signal had already taken out is put back, without a block update), a dispenser's TNT item stays in it. Not asked: TNT set off by a blast (`native_explosion_detonate` spares blocks), a TNT minecart and a sulfur cube. Server-side and in single player. 181. |
| `toast_add` | — | cancel |  | NeoForge's `ToastAddEvent`: a new toast is about to be queued. `kind` is `advancement`, `recipe`, `tutorial`, `system` or `now_playing`; `id` is the advancement id, the first recipe id, the tutorial hint (`move`, `look`, `find_tree`, `punch_tree`, `open_inventory`, `craft_planks`, `socialInteractions`), the system toast's id (`narrator_toggle`, `pack_load_failure`, `pack_download`, `low_disk_space`, `chunk_load_failure`, `chunk_save_failure`), or empty for `now_playing`. An update to a toast already queued or shown is not an add. Set `cancel` and it isn't queued, shown or sounded. Title-screen toasts are not told. Client-side. API @API:toast_add@. |
| `tooltip` | 12 | collect |  | An item's tooltip, wherever the game shows one (slots, the creative tabs, the recipe book, chat's hover): the stack, with its components (`stack.data()`: a shulker box's contents...), and its lines, the name first, each with a colour as `rgba` packs it (`u32::MAX` keeps the text's own). Add, change or take out lines; `Text::legacy` reads `§` codes. Asked each frame the tooltip shows, never for one the stack hides. API 12. |
| `tooltip_color` | — | listen |  | Change a tooltip box's background and border gradient colors, as ARGB. Stack is None for tooltips not associated with an item. |
| `tooltip_component` | — | replace |  | Client-side image component for this stack's tooltip. Answer its width/height in GUI pixels; finite positive dimensions reserve space after text and any vanilla bundle component. None keeps the vanilla tooltip unchanged. |
| `tooltip_component_draw` | — | listen |  | Render the measured component at origin, inside the tooltip background. Stack is the component's data. Use native_sprite/native_fill/native_text; size is the measurement returned by native_tooltip_component this frame. |
| `tooltip_render_pre` | — | cancel |  | Intercept item tooltip rendering before geometry calculation and drawing. Setting `cancel` to true suppresses vanilla tooltip rendering. |
| `trade_select` | — | listen |  | A server player selected trade `index` from `villager` in the trading menu. 302. |
| `trade_with_villager` | 310 | listen |  | A server player traded with a villager or a wandering trader (NeoForge's `TradeWithVillagerEvent`, at vanilla's `MerchantResultSlot.onTake` once the offer is taken): `merchant` is the trader's entity id and `kind` its type (`minecraft:villager`, `minecraft:wandering_trader`), `offer` the trade as it is after this one (its `uses` counted, `result` what the player got). Once per trade, so a shift-click that trades several times is heard for each, after the trade's statistic and `villager_trade` trigger. Listen only: the trade is made. The player's state is swapped in (`native_acting_player`). API 310. |
| `trample` | — | cancel |  | An entity is about to trample farmland (NeoForge's `FarmlandTrampleEvent`, Bukkit's `PlayerInteractEvent` with `Action.PHYSICAL` for a player and `EntityInteractEvent` for a mob): `entity` (its network id; a player's is the one their client knows) of type `kind` (`minecraft:player`, `minecraft:zombie`...) fell `fall_distance` blocks onto the farmland at `pos` in `dimension`, and vanilla's checks have let it (`FarmlandBlock.fallOn`: the chance from the fall, a living entity big enough, `mob_griefing` for a mob). Set `cancel` and the farmland stays, the crop on it too; the fall damage is taken either way. There is no `self`: the game is in the middle of the entity's move. Server-side. @API:trample@. |
| `update_shape` | — | replace |  | An authoritative server is about to compute the state the block `state` at `pos` takes now that its neighbour in `direction` is `neighbour` (`BlockBehaviour.updateShape`). `state` may not be in the world yet (a piston landing it): decide from `state`, not from the block at `pos`. Answer only for your own blocks: put the new state in `new` (`state` keeps the block as it is; air breaks it, with its drops, on a neighbour update) and the block's own `updateShape` doesn't run, nor the ticks it would schedule. The level is read-only, as vanilla's `LevelReader`; ticks go through `native_schedule_block_tick` and `native_schedule_fluid_tick` with `ticks` (`ScheduledTickAccess`). It runs often, at least six times per `setBlock` that updates shapes (more for redstone wire's diagonals and knock-on updates): keep it short. |
| `use_animation` | 90 | listen |  | `Item.getUseAnimation` of `stack` in use, for the first person hand: `animation` arrives with its consumable's (`eat`, `drink`), else `None`. `Eat` and `Drink` bring the food to the mouth, `Bow` draws, `Trident` raises, `Brush` sweeps; the rest hold the item still. Asked each frame the hand draws an item in use, for an item with no pose of its own (bows, crossbows, tridents, brushes and spears keep theirs). Client-side. API 90. |
| `use_duration` | 90 | listen |  | `Item.getUseDuration` of `stack`, in ticks: `duration` arrives with vanilla's (a consumable's time, 72000 for a shield, a spear, a bow, 0 for an item with no use over time). A mod's own item (outside `minecraft:`) with no `consumable`, `blocks_attacks` or kinetic weapon that answers above 0 is used over time on a right click, as an `Item.use` that calls `startUsingItem`, until it is let go or the time runs out (`native_living_entity_use_item_finish`). A consumable's time changes too, potions and the other vanilla items keep their own. Asked when a use starts, each tick a mod's item is in use, and each frame the hand draws one in use, on both sides. It has no user, as it is asked so often: answer from the stack alone. API 90. |
| `use_item` | 13 | cancel | `item_use(item, player)`, by item | A player uses `stack` (right click) with `self.hand`: in the air, or on a block once `native_use_item_on` let it through, where `Item.use` starts. Each click reaches it once. Set `claimed` to take the use: the hand swings and the item's own use doesn't run. Server-side, for every player of the world; an item on cooldown is never used. API 13. |
| `use_item_on` | 13 | cancel | `item_use_on(item, player, block, face)`, by item | A player uses `stack` (right click) with `self.hand` on the block at `pos`, `face` the face clicked (`[0, 1, 0]` is the top), once the block itself let the click through (a chest still opens): where `ItemStack.useOn` starts. Set `claimed` to take the use: the hand swings and neither the item's `useOn` nor its `use` runs. Server-side, for every player of the world (the helpers read the acting one); an item on cooldown is never used. API 13. |
| `vault_change_state` | — | listen |  | A vault at `pos` changed to `state`. Its block state is updated. Server-side. 303. |
| `vault_loot` | — | listen |  | A vault at `pos` is about to eject a loot item. 353. |
| `vehicle_create` | — | listen |  | A boat or minecart was created at `pos`, after it joined the level. `kind` is the vehicle type. Server-side. 336. |
| `vehicle_damage` | — | cancel |  | A vehicle is about to take damage from a player's attack. `kind` is `boat` or the minecart type; mods may change `damage` or set `cancel` to leave its damage and wobble unchanged. The attack itself still completes. Server-side. 337. |
| `vehicle_destroy` | — | listen |  | A boat or minecart is about to be destroyed at `pos`. TNT minecarts that prime instead of breaking are not heard. Server-side. 338. |
| `vehicle_moved` | — | listen |  | A boat or minecart (`kind`, `minecraft:oak_boat`) moved since the last tick (`VehicleMoveEvent`): `from` and `to` are its positions, heard after the tick moved it. Once a tick for each vehicle that carries a server player, whose state is then swapped in (as for `native_perform_command`: `native_acting_player`, `native_tell` and the item helpers reach them; `player` is their UUID), and for one a server player rode and left, until it has stood still for ten seconds (`player` is none, nobody is swapped in). It only hears. Cheap when nothing moves: one position compare a tick for each watched vehicle. Not heard: a vehicle moved before anyone rode it, a mount (horse, pig...) or a vehicle carrying only a mob. Server-side, in the level the vehicle is in. 178. |
| `vehicle_moved_v2` | — | cancel |  | `native_vehicle_moved` with the vehicle and a say on its move (Bukkit's `VehicleMoveEvent` with a teleport of the vehicle): heard right after v1, at the same times and with the same state swapped in, and also for a mob a server player rides (a horse, a pig, a strider), which v1 does not hear. `dimension` is the level the vehicle is in and `vehicle` its entity id (`native_teleport_vehicle`). Set `cancel` and the vehicle is put back at `from` with its riders; change `to` and it is put there instead (not checked against the blocks; a value that is not finite is ignored). Either way its riders' clients are told, and the next move is heard from there. Mods are asked in order and share `to` and `cancel`. Server-side. API @API:vehicle_moved_v2@. |
| `village_siege` | — | cancel |  | A village siege found a spawn position on the server. Set `canceled` to stop the siege. There is one siege per dimension. 389. |
| `visuals` | — | listen |  | The world frame's local visual sources. Push requests; Horizon validates and limits them before rendering, each mod within its own budget (256 rims and 4096 rim edges, 8 lights). Called only while a world is visible. |
| `weather_change` | — | cancel |  | The server changed its weather parameters. `raining` and `thundering` are the requested final states. Set `cancel` to keep the previous weather parameters. Server-side. 304. |
| `wheel` | — | cancel |  | Wheel steps while playing: set `claimed` to keep them from the hotbar. |
| `whitelist_state_update` | — | listen |  | The dedicated server's whitelist changed to `enabled`. 305. |
| `world_border_bounds_change_finish` | — | listen |  | A timed world-border size change finished on the server, after its final size was applied. Server-side, including the single-player server. 354. |
| `world_border_bounds_changed` | — | listen |  | The server world's border bounds changed, either immediately or when its timed size change was requested. 245. |
| `world_border_center_changed` | — | listen |  | The server world's border center changed. 246. |
| `world_drawn` | — | listen |  | The world is drawn (see [`WorldDrawn`]). Not called on the title screen's panorama. |
| `world_game_rule_change` | — | listen |  | A server game rule changed to its final `value`. 247. |
| `world_lifecycle` | — | listen | `world_lifecycle(phase)` | The world's phases, read-only; `error_text` carries the engine's own open-failure text, empty otherwise. Server-side. A server loop or final save failure fires `WorldCloseFailed` with the error text. |
| `world_primitives` | — | collect |  | Once a frame while the world is drawn, `partial` ticks past the last tick (0 to 1), the camera at `camera`: add lines, box outlines, filled boxes, beacon-style beams and text facing the camera, in world coordinates, to `primitives`, each depth tested or seen through walls (`horizon_client::world_primitives`). Horizon draws them with its own pipelines after the entities and before the first-person hand, at the world's resolution, depth and TAA. Not on the title screen. API @API:world_primitives@. |
| `world_saved` | — | listen |  | The server completed a world save cycle. `wait` says chunk writes were flushed before returning. 306. |
| `world_submit` | — | listen |  | Submit depth-tested world text and textured quads, after particles and before the hand/HUD. The pose starts camera-relative; use `draw.translate_world` for a world position. Called independently of block entities and chunks, so transient overlays may outlive their source block. API @API:world_canvas@. |
| `zoom` | — | replace |  | The zoom a native mod asks for, applied while playing (the spyglass's own view wins): set `zoom` when it is none yet. |

## Host helpers

| Helper | API | Lua | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acting_player` | 21 | `player` in the hooks of a player's action | The player whose action or command a hook hears, as their state is swapped in (`native_perform_command`, `native_right_click_block`, `native_use_item_on`, `native_destroy_block`...): None outside such a hook. API 21. What the hub keeps of them alone (`latency`, `nickname`, `hidden`, `address`) reads as 0 or None while the hub is out of reach. |
| `action_bar` | 21 |  | A line over that player's hotbar (the action bar), also inside a player's hook for the acting player; false when they aren't on. API 21. |
| `add_effect` | — |  | Gives the player `uuid` `effect` as vanilla's `LivingEntity.addEffect` (Bukkit's `addPotionEffect`): it takes the place of a weaker or shorter one of the same kind, which waits under it. Their client gets `UpdateMobEffect` with the ambient and particle flags. Whether anything changed; false also for an unknown effect, a duration of 0 or below -1, a player not reached, and a dead one. API @API:player_effects@. |
| `add_particle` | — |  | `ClientLevel.addParticle`: request one particle in this client's loaded world. Options and provider input slots pass through unchanged, including encoded color or size values in `velocity`. Normal distance, settings and population limits still apply. True means submitted, not necessarily visible: an unknown provider or missing sprite set draws nothing. False on a server, without a client player/level, or for non-finite numeric input. API @API:client_particles@. |
| `apply_screen_blur` | — |  | Requests vanilla's menu background blur for this frame, with a per-frame guard so blur is applied at most once per frame. Returns true if blur was newly requested this frame, or false if it was already applied/requested this frame. API @API:screen_transparent_background@. |
| `attachments` | — | `data` on a mob, `horizon.world_data()`, `horizon.player_data(player)` | Access a server-owned holder's attachment map. On a client it is the copy of what the server synced: `set` and `remove` change only the copy. |
| `attribute` | — |  | The player `uuid`'s attribute `attribute` (`minecraft:max_health`, `scale`): its base value and its value with every modifier (armour, effects, `/attribute`), as Bukkit's `AttributeInstance.getBaseValue` and `getValue`. None for an attribute players don't have, and for a player not reached or between bodies (just respawned, not yet ticked). API @API:player_attributes@. |
| `bake_layer` | — |  | Entity model layer `layer` baked into its `ModelPart` tree, each part at its pose, as `EntityModelSet.bakeLayer` bakes it: one a native mod registered (`native_layer_definitions`), or vanilla's, by the name `entity-models.json` gives it (`minecraft:zombie#main`, `minecraft:player#main`). The tree is the caller's own copy: bake it once, as a renderer does, and set its parts' poses each frame. None for a layer neither has. A vanilla layer no mob has (a player's, a chest's) is read from the resources each call, so slow. API @API:model_layers@. |
| `biome_name` | — |  | The name of biome id `biome` (`minecraft:plains`), as a snapshot's `noise_biome` gives it. None for an unknown id. API @API:chunk_snapshot@. |
| `biome_tint` | — |  | The tints of biome id `biome` at block column `x, z`, each 0xRRGGBB: grass (`Biome.getGrassColor`, with the dark forest's and the swamp's modifiers), foliage, dry foliage and water, after `native_biome_colors`. The biome's own, not blended over the biome blend radius as the client draws them. None for an unknown id. API @API:chunk_snapshot@. |
| `block` | 20 | `horizon.block(x, y, z)` | The block at `pos` (`mymod:cable`; air where nothing is loaded). API 20. |
| `block_collision` | — |  | Collision boxes in block-local coordinates with an empty collision context. |

True when the blow was dealt (whether it hurt is the damage hooks' to tell); false for a level not loaded, no such living mob or target, the mob itself, or a player while a guest's packet is handled (the hub is taken out then). API @API:npc_mob_attack@. |
| `mob_cost_sampling` | — |  | Time every mob's own tick (its riders inside it) from now on, or no longer, summed by level and mob type for `native_take_mob_costs`: two clock reads and a map update a mob while on, one thread-local read off. Sampled apart from a performance report's, so both can run. For a lighter profile, turn it on in `ServerTickStart` of one tick in N and off after. Call it from a server hook (it belongs to the server thread). API @API:server_tick_timed@. |
| `mob_effect` | 366 | `horizon.effect(id, name, ticks[, amplifier])` | Gives the living mob `id` the effect `effect` (`minecraft:speed`) for `ticks` ticks (-1: forever) at `amplifier`, as `/effect give` does on a mob (`LivingEntity.addEffect`): a stronger one replaces what it has, an equal one extends it, a weaker one is kept hidden. False for no such living mob, another dimension, or an effect the game doesn't have. API 366. |
| `mob_follow` | — |  | Walks mob `mob` towards where entity `target` (a mob, a player or any other entity of the same level) stands now, as `PathNavigation.moveTo(entity, speed)` does (done within a block). A path to where it is now: to follow it, call it again as it moves (vanilla's follow and attack goals ask every few ticks). False as `native_mob_navigate`, or for no such target in that level. API @API:npc_mob_navigation@. |
| `mob_look_at` | — |  | Turns mob `mob`'s head towards `at` at its own head speeds, as `LookControl.setLookAt(x, y, z)` does: the head turns on the mob's next tick and the body follows it, as for vanilla's look goals. It holds for that tick only, so call it each tick to keep looking; a mob with `no_ai` doesn't turn (`native_set_entity_rotation` turns it). False for a level not loaded, no such living mob or a point that isn't finite. API @API:npc_mob_navigation@. |
| `mob_navigate` | — |  | Walks mob `mob` of the loaded level `dimension` towards `to` with the engine's pathfinding, as `PathNavigation.moveTo(x, y, z, reach, speed)` does: a path to the block holding `to` (a walker's onto the ground below it), done within `reach` blocks, followed at `speed` times the mob's movement speed. True when a path was found and the mob is on its way; false for no path (within its follow range, as vanilla's), a level not loaded, no such living mob, or a value that isn't finite. The path goes round walls and through open doors as the mob's own navigation allows. The mob's goals may take the navigation over, as they do from vanilla's callers: call it again (an NPC library's navigator does so each tick) or give the mob goals of its own (`native_register_goals`). A mob with `no_ai` keeps the path but doesn't walk it. API @API:npc_mob_navigation@. |
| `mob_navigating` | — |  | Whether mob `mob` is walking a path (`PathNavigation.isInProgress`): false once it arrived, got stuck or was stopped, and for a level not loaded or no such living mob. API @API:npc_mob_navigation@. |
| `mob_stop` | — |  | Stops mob `mob`'s walk (`PathNavigation.stop`): false for a level not loaded or no such living mob. API @API:npc_mob_navigation@. |
| `mob_view` | — | `horizon.mob(id)`, `mob` in the mob hooks | The living mob `id`'s view as its goals see it (`MobView`), in the level in place, `dimension`: none for no such mob or a client's copy. The fields that need the world (`target_position`, `nearby`) are empty. API @API:mob_view@. |
| `mob_views` | — | `horizon.mobs()` | The views of every living mob in the level in place, `dimension`, as `native_mob_view` gives one: none on a client's copy. API @API:mob_views@. |
| `mod_block_entity` | — |  | A copy of the mod block entity at `pos`, to read without changing it: a press reading the basin under it, a client mod drawing a machine from its neighbour's state. On a server, its saved compound, item slots and data slots; on a client, what the server sent of it (`native_block_entity_update_tag`, merged into `nbt`), with no item slots. None for another kind of block entity, a block with none, and on a server for the one ticking now, which is out of the world (as for `native_with_mod_block_entity`). API @API:host_bridge@. |
| `mod_block_entity_data` | — | `data` in the block hooks | The saved compound of the mod block entity at `pos` (`ModBlockEntity.nbt`, without `id`, `x`, `y`, `z` and `Items`): none for no block entity there, a vanilla one, or the one ticking now (out of the world: `native_block_entity_tick` has it). API @API:mod_block_entity_data@. |
| `mod_image` | 355 |  | A mod's own RGBA image, uploaded into the HUD atlas slot [`MOD_IMAGE_SPRITE`](crate::hud::MOD_IMAGE_SPRITE) and drawn with `native_sprite`: its own source rectangle crops and stretches it. `rgba` is `width * height` pixels of four bytes, each side at most [`MOD_IMAGE_SIZE`](crate::hud::MOD_IMAGE_SIZE); false when it is not that size. The upload costs a texture patch of the image, so send one when the image changed, not every frame. API 355. |
| `mod_key` | — |  | The key the player chose for a mod's key `name`, else `default` (`key.keyboard.z`), as the WebAssembly mods' keys were kept (`key.<mod id>.<name>` in `horizon-mods.txt`). |
| `mod_screen` | 111 |  | The mod whose own screen is open, if one is (Escape, or another screen replacing it, closes it). API 111. |
| `mod_screen_close` | 111 |  | Closes mod `mod_id`'s own screen, if it is open. API 111. |
| `mod_screen_open` | 111 |  | Opens a screen of mod `mod_id`'s own over the world: the screen hooks fire over it as over any other, so the mod draws it in `native_screen_render_post` and takes its clicks, scroll, keys and typing there; the mouse is freed, and Escape closes it. Every mod's own screen has the `NativeScreenView.id` `mod`, so a mod's screen hooks check `native_mod_screen()` is its own before drawing. It doesn't pause a single-player game (as the inventory doesn't). True when it is open: false while another screen is (or another mod's), over the title screen, a book, a sign editor, a dialog or a prompt, while the world loads, and anywhere but the window's own client (the server thread, a dedicated server). A gamepad can close it (B, Start) but not click on it: its clicks don't reach the mouse hooks. API 111. |
| `mount` | — |  | Seats the entity `entity` (a server player or a mob) on the vehicle `vehicle` (a boat, a minecart or a mob), as `/ride <entity> mount <vehicle>` does (Bukkit's `Entity.addPassenger`), with its checks: neither rides already, no loop, a free seat, minecarts carry players only, and `native_entity_mount` may refuse. Both in the level in place. Inside a player's hook only the acting player and mobs are reached. True when it rides now; false otherwise and on a client. API @API:mount@. |
| `move_entity` | 59 |  | Moves entity `id`, one Horizon keeps without simulating (a display, a marker, an interaction), to `pos` facing `yaw` and `pitch` in degrees; a display eases there over its `teleport` ticks. False for no such entity, another dimension or a position outside `/summon`'s bounds. Mobs move with `native_teleport_mob`. API 59. |
| `move_fluids` | 55 |  | Moves up to `max` millibuckets from the block at `from`, through its side `from_face`, into the one at `to`, through its side `to_face`, as `native_move_items` moves items: what the target won't take goes back into the source, so none is lost — a cauldron's whole thirds included. The fluid and how much moved; none where `native_fluid_tanks` is none at `from`, where nothing drainable is, where no block holds fluids at `to` or it has no room for that fluid (a tank that refuses it, `native_block_entity_accepts_fluid`, has none), and within one block. The source is asked for no more than the target's room. API 55. |
| `move_items` | 48 |  | Moves up to `max` items from the container at `from`, through its side `from_face`, into the one at `to`, through its side `to_face`, one by one as a hopper does: an item the target refuses stays in its slot, so none is lost. `item` (`minecraft:coal`) takes only that item. How many moved: 0 where `native_container_slots` is none at `from`, where no container is at `to`, and within one container. A composter takes one a call. API 48. |
| `neighbor_signal` | 96 |  | The strongest redstone signal reaching the block at `pos` from its six neighbours, 0 to 15 (`SignalGetter.getBestNeighborSignal`, what a dispenser or a piston reads), in the level in place, `dimension`. 0 on a client's copy of the world and for another dimension. A mod's explosive, launcher or machine reads it in its block entity's tick to go off or switch on. API 96. |
| `net_send_to_player` | 40 |  | Sends `data` on `channel` (`mod_id:name`, at most 30 000 bytes, at most 32 a player a tick) to `player`'s client, at the tick's end, from any server hook. Ok means accepted: a player who left or isn't on a Horizon client doesn't get it. API 40. |
| `net_send_to_server` | 40 |  | The client half: sends `data` on `channel` to the server (the same caps, 32 a tick). An error when the server doesn't carry mod messages (a vanilla server), and until the player has joined: a server says it carries them during configuration, before it can take one. API 40. |
| `new_map` | — |  | A new map of the world showing `colors` (128 x 128 `MapColor` ids times 4 plus the shade, row by row), scale 0, locked as a cartography table locks one (no exploring draws over it) and without player markers, of the level `dimension`: Bukkit's `Server.createMap` with its picture drawn. It takes the world's next map id (`last_id.dat`), is saved with the world's maps and goes, like any map, to whoever carries it or sees it framed, players who join later included. A `minecraft:filled_map` with this `minecraft:map_id` shows it. None on a client of a server and with no world open. API @API:new_map@. |
| `on` | — |  | Whether the player left mod `mod_id` on in Options > Mods. A mod turned off does nothing (check this first in each hook) until the launcher's next build leaves it out. |
| `open_chat` | — |  | Opens the chat screen with `text` typed in and the cursor at its end, as T and / open it (`ChatScreen` with its initial text): a command macro can fill in `/tp ` for the player to finish. Nothing is sent; the player edits and sends it, or presses Escape. The box keeps its limit (256 characters) and its character filter. An error with no player in a world, or while another screen is open. API @API:open_chat@. |
| `open_menu` | — |  | Opens a chest menu of `rows` rows (1 to 6) titled `title` for the player, showing `items` (by slot, padded with empty ones), in place of the menu they had open: its window id. |
| `open_menu_with_input` | — |  | Opens a chest menu as `native_open_menu` does, whose slots in `input` hold items as a chest's do: the player puts stacks in and takes them out by vanilla's click rules (a shift-click from their inventory fills them, a drag spreads over them), and the menu's other slots stay the mod's to show, their clicks heard by `native_menu_clicked`. `items` fills both; `native_set_menu_items` changes only the shown ones and `native_menu_contents` reads them all. When the menu closes, for any reason, the input slots go to `native_menu_input_closed` and what the mods leave there goes back to the player (`clearContainer`). None for a player not here, or `input` empty or past the rows' slots. API @API:menu_input@. |
| `paint_map` | — |  | Replaces the whole picture of the world's map `map_id` (`MapCanvas` drawn for everyone): saved with the maps and sent in full to everyone carrying it or seeing it framed. An unlocked map is still drawn over where its holders explore, as vanilla's are. False for a map this world never made or saved, and on a client of a server. API @API:new_map@. |
| `panel_items` | — |  | Shows the panel beside container screens with these items (at most 8192), as the game's own slots in pages, with a search box; the player's clicks, searches and keys over items come back as `native_panel_event`. The panel is the last mod's to show one; empty items and no recipe page take yours away, except that an empty reply to a non-empty Search keeps its field editable. A clear outside that event still removes the panel (as when a viewer closes). |
| `particles` | — | `horizon.particles(name, x, y, z[, count, spread, speed])` | Shows `count` particles of the simple type `name` (`minecraft:flame`, `minecraft:happy_villager`; those with data of their own, dust and items, are not here) at `pos` in the level in place, spread by `spread` on each axis and moving up to `speed`, to every player within 32 blocks, as `/particle` does: how many saw them; 0 for a name the game does not know. API @API:particles_titles@. |
| `place_recipe` | — |  | Places a recipe in the open screen's grid as a click in the recipe book does (`ServerboundPlaceRecipePacket`): the inventory's grid or a crafting table's. `all` places as many as the items allow, as with Shift. Refused while no such screen is open and for a recipe the player's book doesn't hold; one missing items shows as a ghost. |
| `play_local_sound` | 83 |  | Plays sound event `sound` (`minecraft:entity.generic.explode`, or a mod's own from its `assets/<id>/sounds.json`) at `at` for this player only, `delay` ticks from now (0 to 1200, a minute): a client mod's sound that waits, as thunder heard after the flash or a blast heard when its shock wave arrives. `volume` past 1 carries farther, as vanilla's attenuation does (16 blocks times the volume). False, with nothing played, on a server or for a value out of range; an event the resources don't have plays nothing, as vanilla's. API 83. |
| `play_sound` | — | `horizon.sound(name, x, y, z[, volume, pitch])` | Plays sound event `sound` at `at` for the players near it in the level in place, as a level hook's `LevelWriteHost::play_sound` does (`Level.playSound` with no player): a machine's hum from its block entity's tick. `source` is the `SoundSource` ordinal (4 for `BLOCKS`). | `play_sound_to` | — |  | Plays `sound` to that player alone, as Bukkit's `Player.playSound`: at `at` in their level, or where they stand when it leaves (None), in `category` (`SoundSource`'s name: `master`, `music`, `record`, `weather`, `block`, `hostile`, `neutral`, `player`, `ambient`, `voice`, `ui`). Nobody else hears it, however near. Names go as for `GameLevel::native_play_sound`: an unknown `minecraft:` event is dropped, another namespace's goes by name. It leaves at the tick's end, so it works from any server hook; true means queued. False on a client, for a bad name, category, position, volume or pitch, and for a player who isn't on (inside another player's hook, where the players are out of reach, such a player just gets nothing). API @API:play_sound_to@. |
| `player` | — |  | The player, in a world. |
| `player_advancements` | — |  | The player's advancement progress as vanilla saves it (`players/advancements/<uuid> .json`: each advancement's obtained criteria with their dates and `done`), as Bukkit's `getAdvancementProgress` reads it. None for a player who is not on and on a client. API @API:player_records@. |
| `player_channels` | — |  | The plugin channels `player`'s client registered (`minecraft:register`, NUL-separated names, in the configuration and in play, less those it unregistered), in the order it registered them: what Bukkit's `Player.getListeningPluginChannels` gives. Empty for a player who isn't on, on a client, and inside a player's own hook, the hub being out then (`native_player_register_channels` names what changed). @API:player_channels@. |
| `player_client` | — |  | What the player's client told the server (brand, `ClientInformation`) and what the server sent it, as Paper's `getClientBrandName`, `locale` and `getClientViewDistance` read it. None for a player who is not on, while the hub is out of reach, and on a client. API @API:player_client@. |
| `player_compound` | — |  | The player `uuid`'s compound as the server would save it now (`players/data/<uuid>.dat`, vanilla's `ServerPlayer.saveWithoutId`): inventory, health, food, experience, effects, attributes, position, and every key Horizon keeps without modelling it. What a mod stores to give the player back elsewhere. None inside a player's turn (their live state is swapped out of their record: call from `native_server_tick`), and for a player not on. API @API:player_compound@. |
| `player_effect` | 367 | `horizon.effect(player, name, ticks[, amplifier])` | Gives the player `uuid` the effect `effect` (`minecraft:regeneration`) for `ticks` ticks (-1: forever) at `amplifier`, as `/effect give` does: a stronger one replaces what they have, an equal one extends it. False, and nothing given, for an effect the game doesn't have, a player who isn't here or is dead, and for another player inside a player's hook, as for `native_give_experience`. API 367. |
| `player_equipment` | — |  | The stack in one of the player's equipment slots (`LivingEntity.getItemBySlot`), from any server hook, the acting player's or another's. None for an empty slot, for `Body` and `Saddle`, for a player who is not on and on a client. API @API:player_equipment@. |
| `player_food` | — |  | The player `uuid`'s food level (0 to 20), saturation and exhaustion, as vanilla's `FoodData` holds them. None for a player not reached. API @API:player_status@. |
| `player_head` | — |  | A player head of the player `uuid` (Bukkit's `SkullMeta.setOwningPlayer`): its `minecraft:profile` holds their id, and their name and properties (the skin) when they are on and the hub is in reach, so it shows their skin at once (else their name from the profile cache, if there); a profile without properties the client resolves itself. API @API:player_textures@. |
| `player_permission` | — |  | The permission level of a player who is on the server or joining it: 0 to 4, an operator's from `ops.json` above 0 (`PlayerList.getProfilePermissions`; a single player world's guests get 2 with cheats on). Inside a player's hook, with the hub out of reach, only that player is found. None for a player who isn't on, and on a client. API @API:player_permission@. |
| `player_persistent_data` | — |  | The compound mods keep on the player `uuid` (NeoForge's `Entity.getPersistentData()`, Bukkit's `PersistentDataContainer`): saved in their file as `NeoForgeData`, beside the keys Horizon keeps without modelling them; an empty compound when there is none. None for a player not reached. API @API:player_persistent_data@. |
| `player_raycast` | — | `horizon.raycast(player, distance)` | The first block within `distance` (at most `RAYCAST_MAX`) along the look of the server player `uuid`, from their eyes: what they point at. None for a player who is not on, or nothing within the loaded chunks. API @API:mob_views@. |
| `player_sneaking` | — |  | Whether the player `uuid` holds sneak (`Player.isShiftKeyDown`): a hub guest's from the hub, the window's own player's (or the guest whose state is swapped in for their action) from their pose. None for a player the game doesn't know. API @API:dev_helpers@. |
| `player_stacks` | — | `horizon.inventory(player)`, `horizon.count_items(player, id)`, `horizon.carried_items(player)` | The player's 36 inventory slots (0..9 the hotbar), to show or offer them; None for a player not here, dead, or whose state is swapped in. |
| `player_stat` | — |  | One statistic of the player: its type and key (`minecraft:custom`, `minecraft:jump`; `custom`, `jump` mean the same), 0 when never counted. None for a player who is not on and on a client. API @API:player_records@. |
| `player_stats` | — |  | The player's statistics as vanilla saves them (`players/stats/<uuid>.json`: `{"stats": {"minecraft:custom": {"minecraft:jump": 3}}, "DataVersion": ..}`), as Bukkit's `getStatistic` reads them. None for a player who is not on and on a client. API @API:player_records@. |
| `player_textures` | — |  | The `textures` property of a player who is on (Paper's `Player.getPlayerProfile`): its value (base64 JSON naming the skin and cape) and signature (None unsigned), as their player list entry carries it, `native_set_profile_property`'s edits included. | `player_view_distance` | — |  | The view distance the player `uuid` has now: the radius of chunks it is sent (`native_set_player_view_distance`). None off a server, for a player not online, and inside a guest's packet hook. API @API:player_view_distance@. |
| `playing` | — |  | Playing, with nothing over the world: keys and zoom apply. API @API:extras_helpers@. |
| `poll` | 116 |  | Mod `mod_id`'s events since its last poll (at most 256 wait). API 116. |
| `pop_resource_pack` | — |  | Takes the pack `id` away from `player`'s client, or every server pack it has for None (`ClientboundResourcePackPopPacket`, Bukkit's `Player.removeResourcePack` and `removeResourcePacks`); the client reloads without it. | `profile_by_name` | — |  | A player the server knows by name, any case (Bukkit's `getOfflinePlayer` without its network lookup, vanilla's `GameProfileCache.get`): one who is on, else one in a dedicated server's profile cache (`usercache.json`: who joined in the last month, and names its commands looked up).
