| `profile_by_uuid` | — |  | The name of the player `uuid`: one who is on, else one in a dedicated server's profile cache, as `native_profile_by_name`. API @API:profile_cache@. |
| `push_mob` | 37 | `horizon.push_mob(dimension, id, x, y, z)` | Adds `velocity` to mob `id`'s: false for no such mob, another dimension or a velocity that isn't finite. API 37. |
| `push_player` | 105 |  | For a client mod: a push added to the local player's velocity, in blocks a tick, as an explosion's knockback is (the window's player moves itself, as vanilla's client does). Each component is clamped to -4..4; a spectator, or a value that is not a number, is left alone. API 105. |
| `quad` | 111 |  | A quad of corners `points` (in order round it) in GUI pixels, `argb`: a wedge, a slanted bar, what `native_fill`'s rectangles can't draw. API 111. |
| `raycast` | 116 |  | The first block along the view within `distance` (at most 1024), past the loaded chunks over the distant terrain. API 116. |
| `read_columns` | 127 |  | For a server mod: `below` blocks under and `above` blocks from each column's height by `heightmap`, as a palette and indexes, with the biome's grass, foliage and water tints (air outside the column and in columns not loaded). The tints are the biome's at the column's top, not blended over the biome blend radius as the game draws them: near a biome border they can differ from what players see. `Err` says why nothing was read: another dimension or a client of a server, `below + above` of 0 or more than the level's height, or a read of more than 1,048,576 blocks (`MAX_READ`; it runs on the server tick, so read big areas in pieces). API 127. |
| `recipe_book_category` | — |  | The validated category and icon of a custom recipe type, or None for an undeclared/invalid type, before resources load, or outside a world. Rebuilt when the recipe table changes. Does not unlock any recipes. |
| `recipe_ingredient` | 36 |  | An ingredient as a recipe's JSON names it: an item, a `#tag`, or a list of them, a bare id as `minecraft:` (as vanilla reads it); `test` says whether a stack fits. | `recipe_result` | 36 |  | A stack as a recipe's `result` names it: `id` (a bare one as `minecraft:`), `count` (1 by default, up to 99) and `components`. None without an `id`, for an item the game doesn't know or a count outside that, and outside a world. API 36. |
| `recipes_of_type` | 36 |  | The recipes of type `kind` (`mymod:crusher`), a type outside `minecraft`, from `data/<namespace>/recipe/*.json` of the content mods (`.hmod`) and the world's data packs, in file order: each one's id and its file as JSON, for the mod to read as it likes. These are the server's table on the server thread, a dedicated server or a LAN host; a client, the single-player window included, sees only the content mods' recipes, not the world's data packs', unless a mod had the server send it the type (`native_datapack_sync`). API 36. |
| `refresh_biome_colors` | 107 |  | Asks `native_biome_colors` again for every biome and, when the colours differ from those in use, rebuilds every loaded section and the far terrain with them (`LevelRenderer.allChanged`, as changing Biome Blend does). | `refresh_commands` | — |  | A mod changed the commands it registers (`native_register_commands`): at the start of the next server tick every mod is asked again, the commands players may run are rebuilt, and every player on the server is sent their tree again, after `native_player_commands_sent`. Nothing happens where no world is open to players, and nothing for a server whose mods never call it. API @API:refresh_commands@. |
| `refresh_player` | — |  | Shows an online player again with their current profile (Paper's `hidePlayer` then `showPlayer`, plus the player's own respawn): every player who sees them gets their list entry anew and their entity again, and the player is respawned in place into the level they are in (all their state kept), so their own client draws a new skin too. Queued for the end of their level's pass, so it works from any server hook; once a tick at most. A dead player is only shown again to the others (their respawn shows them the rest). False on a client; true does not mean the player was found. API @API:profile_refresh@. |
| `remove_component` | — |  | Remove a native component, including its item default. |
| `remove_effect` | — |  | Takes the effect `id` off the player `uuid`, as `/effect clear`: whether they had it. API @API:player_effects@. |
| `remove_entity` | 59 |  | Removes entity `id`, one Horizon keeps without simulating, as `/kill` does (it drops nothing and isn't saved). False for no such entity or another dimension. Mobs go with `native_remove_mob`. API 59. Since API @API:remove_projectiles@ it also takes projectiles (arrows, tridents, snowballs, eggs, pearls, fireballs, wind charges, llama spit, shulker bullets, firework rockets) as `/kill` does, and a server player's fishing bobber (`Entity.discard`; the player in place's, or, outside a guest's turn, any of this level's players'). |
| `remove_mob` | 37 | `horizon.remove_mob(dimension, id)` | Takes mob `id` out of the world with no death and no loot: false for no such mob or another dimension. API 37. |
| `resend_commands` | — |  | Sends a player their command tree again, the mods asked anew (`native_player_commands_sent`, its v2 and the permission nodes of the mods' commands), as Bukkit's `Player.updateCommands`: after a permissions mod changed what they may use. It goes in the next server tick, so it works from any server hook, the player's own included (from the commands-sent hooks themselves it would send it every tick). True when the player is on (or is the acting player); false for anyone else and on a client. API @API:resend_commands@. |
| `reserve_entity_id` | — |  | An entity id no entity of this server will take (`Entity.nextEntityId`'s counter), for a mod's own packets to a client. API @API:client_entities@. |
| `respawn_player` | — |  | Respawns the dead server player `uuid` as their client's Respawn click does (Spigot's `player.spigot().respawn()`, `ClientCommand` `PERFORM_RESPAWN`): at their bed, anchor or the world spawn, with `native_player_respawned` and the respawn hooks, without waiting for the click. Done after the players' packets of the server tick (the same tick from a packet's hook or the tick's start, else the next). True when queued; false for a player seen not on the server or alive (inside a player's hook nobody else can be seen: it is queued, and does nothing for a living player), and on a client. API @API:respawn_player@. |
| `room_for` | — |  | How many plain `item` still fit; 0 for an unknown item. |
| `run_command` | 21 | `horizon.run_command(line)` | Runs `line` (no slash) as the server's console does: permission level 4, from the overworld's spawn, with no output. A teleport to another level (`execute in minecraft:the_nether run tp Alex 0 70 0`) happens at the next tick's start, as the console's. Whether it ran without failing. Only where no player's state is swapped in (`native_tick`, `native_menu_clicked`): false inside a player's hook, where the other players are out of reach. API 21. |
| `run_command_as` | — |  | Runs `line` (a leading slash allowed) as the player `uuid` typing it would (Bukkit's `Player.performCommand`): their source, operator level and position, a command a mod registered going to the mods (`native_perform_command`) when their level allows it. Its answer is sent to them as their own command's, and its lines also come back in `output`. `native_player_command` doesn't hear it. Where `native_run_command` runs, or inside that player's own hook (then the lines join the hook's feedback); elsewhere, or for a player not on the server, nothing runs. API @API:run_command_as@. |
| `run_command_as_owner` | — |  | Runs a command as the world's owner, in the owner's level, at the owner's permission level, and returns the chat replies. API @API:lua_console_helpers@. |
| `run_command_captured` | — |  | `native_run_command` with its answer kept, as vanilla's `CommandSourceStack.withCallback` on a source that keeps what it is sent: `line` (a leading slash allowed) runs as the console, a command a mod registered going to the mods (`native_perform_console_command`), anything else to vanilla's. The lines it answers with come back in `output` and reach no one else, operators included. Only where `native_run_command` runs: inside a player's hook nothing runs. API @API:run_command_captured@. |
| `run_mod_command` | — |  | `native_run_command` that reaches the mods' commands too (Bukkit's `Bukkit.dispatchCommand` from the console): a command a mod registered goes to the mods (`native_perform_console_command`), anything else to vanilla's. Whether it ran: a mod took it, or vanilla's ran without failing. No output, as `native_run_command`. API @API:run_mod_command@. |

| `screen_pos` | — |  | The block of the mod screen that is open (`native_screen`), as the server named it when the block opened its menu type; None when no mod screen is open. 401. |

Ok means queued: a player who isn't on by then gets nothing. Nothing counts these; the bytes are the mod's to get right. An error on a client, and for a bad channel or size. API @API:send_custom_payload_to_player@. |

| `send_packet` | 409 |  | Sends `packet` to the server as it is, to any server, a vanilla one included: a plugin channel's payload (`ServerboundCustomPayloadPacket`) or any other play packet. An error when the player isn't in a server's play state, and for a custom payload past `ServerboundCustomPayloadPacket.MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE`, which a server disconnects for. API 409. |

| `send_particles_to` | — |  | Shows particles to that player alone, as Bukkit's `Player.spawnParticle` and vanilla's `ServerLevel.sendParticles(player, ...)` (`/particle ... force\|normal <player>`): `count` of them around `at` in their level, spread by `spread`, at `speed` (0 sends one directional particle, as `GameLevel::native_send_particles`). It leaves at the tick's end, so it works from any server hook; true means queued. | `send_resource_pack` | — |  | Offers `player`'s client the resource pack at `url` (Bukkit's `Player.addResourcePack`): `ClientboundResourcePackPushPacket` with the pack's own `id` (a UUID the mod picks, so it can pop that pack again and match the answers `native_resource_pack_status_v2` gets), `sha1` its lowercase hex hash (empty: the client doesn't check it), the prompt's extra line and whether the client calls it required. None for a block the game doesn't have, a property it hasn't, or block NBT (`{...}`, not read here). API 365. |

None on a client's copy of the world, for a position outside `/summon`'s bounds, a chunk that isn't loaded, a kind Horizon can't load, or one a mod kept out (`native_entity_join_level`). API 59. Since API @API:npc_any_level@, `dimension` may be any level the server has loaded, which is put in place for the summon (`execute in <dimension> run summon`); a level not loaded is refused. |

| `teleport_player` | — |  | Teleports the server player `uuid` to `pos` in `dimension` (`minecraft:the_nether`), facing `yaw` and `pitch` in degrees, as `/tp` does (Bukkit's `Player.teleport`): they leave their vehicle, lose their motion and fall, and their client is told. Callable from any server hook. Within their level it is done at once when they are the acting player or nobody's state is swapped in (a tick hook); inside another player's hook, where the other players are out of reach, it is done after the players' packets of the server tick (the same tick when the hook heard a packet). Into another level it happens when the tick's level teleports run, as a command's does. True when it is done or queued; false for a player not on the server or dead (when that can be seen), a dimension other than the three, a position outside `/tp`'s bounds, an angle that is not finite, and on a client. API @API:teleport_player@. |

A mob that rides something itself leaves it. Only where nobody's state is swapped in (a tick hook, a vehicle's hook nobody rides; inside `native_vehicle_moved_v2` a mod changes `to` instead): false inside a player's hook, for no such vehicle here, another dimension, a position outside `/tp`'s bounds, and on a client. API @API:teleport_vehicle@. |

| `use_as_player` | — |  | Uses `stack` as a player standing with its eyes at `eye`, looking `yaw` and `pitch` degrees (as `Entity.getYRot` and `getXRot`), would: NeoForge's `FakePlayer` doing what a deployer does. On a block (`NativeUseTarget::Block`) it is `ServerPlayerGameMode.useItemOn`: the block reacts first (a lever flips, a cauldron fills), else the item is used on it (a block placed, bone meal spread, a bucket filled); in the air (`Item`) `useItem` (a bucket picks up the fluid it looks at); on an entity (`Entity`) `Player.interactOn` (a sheep sheared, a cow milked). With `sneaking` it is a secondary use, as a player holding sneak's. The fake player is in survival, holds `stack` in its main hand and nothing else, and has no connection: what it opens closes again through the real close paths before this returns (a lid opens and shuts, a trader is free again), and its stats and advancements count for no one. The click still counts as used, as a player's would. The answer is what it holds and carries afterwards. None, with nothing used, off a server and while a player's action is being run (from inside a player's hook: run it from a block entity's tick). API @API:fake_player@. |
